note: S$ addressable is before conversion: drop-off S$ is the account's last-12-month value at risk (assumed save rate 25%); cross-sell S$ is the yearly gap to similar customers (assumed conversion 15%); blocked requests are delayed, not new, revenue. Never summed into a revenue headline. Signals run on merged customers: on raw SAP records the same rules would miss 7 real drop-offs and raise 12 false alarms.

cards.implication: Singapore grew +2.5% to S$17.1M (+0.5% in Jul–Sep), but test kits are flat (−0.4%) because of a weak dengue season (dengue kits −13%, other kits +2.9%), not lost customers. Raw SAP overstates Singapore by S$1.06M (6.2%): three Singapore-coded billing records hold Malaysian and Vietnamese hospitals' orders.

cards.implication: Vietnam is the fastest-growing market, +8.9% to S$9.28M (test kits +21%; +24% in Jul–Sep). Yet four public hospitals buy test kits but no consumables (B), and merged, Bệnh viện Đa khoa Hồng Lạc is down 29% after its orders moved to an unaccented duplicate record. Expect the Tet dip: February orders were 36% below January and March this year.
